sentences.text: Gwalior, Dated : 02-12-2019
Shri Prashant Shrama with Harshad Bahirani, learned counsel for applicant.
Shri Purushottam Panday, learned Public Prosecutor for respondent/State.
Case dairy is perused.
This is second bail application u/S 439 of Cr.P.C filed by the applicant for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested on 02.08.2019 by Police Station STF, Bhopal, District (Gwalior Unit) in connection with Crime No.12/2019 registered in relation to the offence punishable u/Ss 420, 272,
273 and 120-B of IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.

I t is alleged by learned counsel for the applicant that earlier bail application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 30.08.2019 passed in M.Cr.C No. 35814/2019 with liberty to repeat after filling of charge sheet.

Now, investigation in the matter is over and charge-sheet has been filed on 24.09.2019, therefore,
no further custodial interrogation may be necessary.

He further submits that the matters relating to Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 have been taken into consideration by the Division Bench of Principal Seat of this Court in W.P. No. 21768/2019 (Sudeep Jain Vs. State of M.P. and Ors.),
whereby the manner in which the proceedings have been taken by the authorities is held to be illegal.

entities.text: Sudeep Jain Vs. State of M.P. and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applicant is ready to abide by all the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
Upon these grounds, he prays for bail.

P er contra, learned counsel for State has opposed the prayer and submits that earlier bail application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 30.08.2019, however, investigation in the matter is over and charge sheet has been filed.
He further submits that merely by filing of charge-sheet does not 2 MCRC-49109-2019 entitle for grant of bail.
He fairly submits that there is no other criminal antecedents against the present applicant.
He prays for dismissal of the bail application.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is second bail application u/S 439 of Cr.P.C filed by the applicant for grant of bail.
The applicant has been arrested on 02.08.2019 by Police Station STF, Bhopal, District (Gwalior Unit) in connection with Crime No.12/2019 registered in relation to the offence punishable u/Ss 420, 272,
273 and 120-B of IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.
Now, investigation in the matter is over and charge-sheet has been filed on 24.09.2019, therefore,
no further custodial interrogation may be necessary.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
He further submits that the matters relating to Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 have been taken into consideration by the Division Bench of Principal Seat of this Court in W.P. No. 21768/2019 (Sudeep Jain Vs. State of M.P. and Ors.),
whereby the manner in which the proceedings have been taken by the authorities is held to be illegal.
He further submits that merely by filing of charge-sheet does not 2 MCRC-49109-2019 entitle for grant of bail.
He fairly submits that there is no other criminal antecedents against the present applicant.
opennyai_summary.decision:
He prays for dismissal of the bail application.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and looking the fact that charge-sheet has been filed, therefore, further custodial interrogation may not be necessary, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case,
this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rs.One Lac Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court.
This order will remain operative subject to compliance of the following conditions by the applicant:-
1. The applicant will comply with all the terms and conditions of the bond executed by him;
2. The applicant will cooperate in the investigation/trial, as the case may be;
3 . The applicant will not indulge himself in extending inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to the Police Officer, as the case may be;
4. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused;
5. The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and 6.
The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
7 . The applicant shall mark his attendance before the concerned police station in the first week of every month, till 3 MCRC-49109-2019 conclusion of investigation (pending if any) and if charge sheet is being filed,
he will mark his presence as per the directions issued by the concerning trial Court.
I n event of failure to comply with any of the terms and conditions, the State authorities will be at liberty to move for cancellation of bail.
A copy of this order be sent to the Court concerned for compliance.
C.c. as per rules.
